candidates.excerpt: The Greenbrier Companies will transition to new executive leadership in January, with Chief Executive and President Lorie Tekorius set to retire following the company’s 2027 annual shareholders meeting. Brian Comstock, Greenbrier’s executive vice president and president of The Americas, will immediately become president and CEO. The Lake Oswego, Ore.-based railcar manufacturer and freight-transportation services provider (NYSE: GBX) said the move is the result of the board’s long-term succession-planning process. Tekorius’ retirement will become effective Jan. 6, 2027. Tekorius has spent more than 30 years at Greenbrier, joining the company in 1995 and moving through senior financial and operating roles before becoming president and CEO in 2022. She previously served as chief operating officer and as chief financial officer. candidates.excerpt: French start-up Velvet, formerly known as Proxima, has obtained its railway undertaking licence from the Direction générale des infrastructures, des transports et des mobilités (DGITM), the company announced on 1 September. This is the first major regulatory approval on its path to launching high-speed services in 2028 between Paris and Bordeaux, Nantes, Angers and Rennes. The licence enables Velvet to progress with path applications, secure infrastructure access agreements and develop its operating procedures. The company, co-founded in 2022 by Rachel Picard — former managing director of SNCF Voyages — and Tim Jackson, founder of Alpha Trains, is backed by Antin Infrastructure Partners, which plans to invest around €1 billion in the project’s first phase. Velvet is already working on its Safety Management System; the next regulatory step will be the Single Safety Certificate.
